primary.thesis: The resolution uses rank on the LMArena text leaderboard with style control off. That metric rewards models that are broadly preferred in head-to-head chat, which tends to favour long, polished, well-formatted answers. Google has held or shared the top rank for most of the leaderboard's recent history (Gemini 2.5 Pro, then Gemini 3 Pro). It also has a fast release cycle, and it has a structural incentive to tune Gemini for Arena-style preference. It usually times a flagship or a 'preview' refresh for Q4, so on December 31 a Gemini model is the likeliest holder of rank 1. Anthropic is the main challenger. Its recent Opus models have ranked at or near the top, and in a tie on rank the alphabetical tiebreak puts 'Anthropic' ahead of 'Google'. Because the other contracts are all NO, the rest of the basket expresses that the frontier is a two-lab race, not a three-lab one: OpenAI's recent flagships have been tuned more for reasoning and agentic benchmarks than for Arena chat preference, and xAI tends to peak briefly after a launch and then fade.

basket.reason: Google has held rank 1 on the no-style-control text board most often, releases Gemini frequently, and has a Q4 release pattern, which makes a Gemini model the default holder of first place on Dec 31.

Anthropic's Opus line has been competing for the top of the Arena text board. Rank ties at the top are common, and the tiebreak on unrounded score, then alphabetical order, can favour Anthropic. This covers a late-2026 Claude flagship overtaking Gemini.
xAI's Grok releases tend to take the top spot briefly and then lose rank as more votes come in and competitors ship. Holding rank 1 on the exact check date needs a very well-timed release.

Open-weight Chinese labs such as DeepSeek have ranked near the frontier but not at rank 1 of the overall text board. Compute export limits make overtaking the US closed-model leaders by year-end unlikely.

failure_narrative: The basket loses if OpenAI or xAI holds rank 1 on December 31. The most plausible path is OpenAI shipping a GPT-5.x or GPT-6-class model in Q4 2026 (for example, timed for the holidays) that is tuned for conversational preference and gains enough early votes to top the board, while Google's next Gemini slips into 2027 and Anthropic's release is aimed at coding and agents rather than chat preference. A second path is xAI launching a new Grok version, trained on the Colossus expansion, in mid-to-late December, so it is at rank 1 on the check date before its score settles. The Google leg also loses if Anthropic ties or beats Gemini, but that case is covered by the Anthropic leg.
hedge_thesis: In the worlds where the primary fails, OpenAI (or xAI) has regained the consumer-perceived frontier in late 2026. Mechanically, a clear OpenAI chat-quality win would come from a large new training run on newly online compute (Stargate sites such as Abilene, plus Microsoft and Oracle capacity). That would show up outside the leaderboard: OpenAI fundraising or valuation headlines, ChatGPT subscriber and usage growth, and stronger sentiment toward OpenAI's infrastructure partners (Oracle, Microsoft, SoftBank, CoreWeave, and the Nvidia GPUs in Stargate). Google's position would look relatively weaker, with Alphabet's 'AI leader' narrative and TPU and Gemini-app momentum stalling. Instruments tied to OpenAI's compute and capital stack would tend to do well in exactly the worlds where Gemini or Claude is not at rank 1.
